evidence_boundary: Calculated and structural statements about a supplied model. They do not establish that the model describes a physical system, and they do not establish novelty; both need comparison with experiment and with the literature.
question: With what exponent does a population whose per-capita growth rate is proportional to its size reach infinity in finite time?
assumptions: the per-capita growth rate n'/n is proportional to n: von Foerster, Mora and Amiot fitted N = 1.79 x 10^11 / (2026.87 - t)^0.99 persons to the world population, and the exponent 0.99 is taken as 1
n in units of 10^9 persons and t in years, so that their constant becomes C = 179
no limit to resources and no noise

provenance.source: H. von Foerster, P. M. Mora and L. W. Amiot, Doomsday: Friday, 13 November, A.D. 2026, Science 132, 1291 (1960)

blowup.verdict: blow-up in finite time: |x| ~ (t* - t)^(-1), predicted by the balance p = 1
